title: SNAP outreach raises take-up while changing the marginal enrollee profile
source_unit: Randomized Pennsylvania older-adult SNAP outreach experiment; treatment and control participants remain source-specific

observations.period: Nine months after randomized 2018 SNAP outreach

denominator.unit: likely-eligible Pennsylvania adults age 60+ not enrolled at baseline

marginal_enrollee_profile.value: lower benefits and less sickness than average control-group enrollee

observations.method: Randomized field experiment assigning likely-eligible older non-enrollees to status quo, eligibility information, or information plus application assistance; administrative enrollment and benefit/health measures.
observations.uncertainty: Historical Pennsylvania experiment; does not identify current national take-up, food security, benefit adequacy, household adaptation, trust, action, or recovery.
observations.subgroup: Likely-eligible Pennsylvania adults age 60+ not enrolled in SNAP at baseline.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower-benefit and better-health marginal profile may reflect information, paperwork, need, health, language, trust, or access differences; the study does not isolate each pathway.

boundary: The experiment closes information/assistance to enrollment and marginal-targeting stages. It does not close benefit adequacy, food security, household adaptation, trust, political action, or recovery.
